To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the beam loading of the rf cavities can be described with high fidelity by a simple numerical model, that the rf controls are capable of handling high current operation, and that the beam current can be increased further by reducing the beam emittance and improving the rf efficiency.

the beam-cavity rf interaction is well described by the numerical model; the beam-cavity system can operate with heavy beam loading; and that the rf control system can operate stably with a beam-cavity interaction that has large transient beam loading.

1) the beam loading of the cavities is dominated by the beam current; 2) the beam loading can be compensated by a combination of rf phase and amplitude changes; 3) the rf control system is able to handle the beam loading and maintain the rf amplitude and phase at a constant level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a numerical model of the beam-cavity system in the CEBAF accelerator.
the design, development, and construction of superconducting radio frequency (rf) cavities, the rf system, and the beam transport system.
the development of the rf control and beam diagnostics systems for a superconducting cw electron accelerator.
